structured_output.summary: The diff implements Array.prototype.fill following the spec steps in order: ToObject, LengthOfArrayLike, ToClampedIndex(start), ToClampedIndex(end) only when end is not undefined, then the Set loop with ToString(k) via key_from_index and Set(..., true) propagated with `?`, returning obj. The local to_clamped_index helper matches ToAbsoluteIndex plus the final clamp, and the ToIntegerOrInfinity call order is correct. No special-casing, swallowed errors, or made-up values. The BigInt failures in the gate report come from the test files themselves, not this code. The only open concern is GC rooting, which is a note rather than a spec defect.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Optional hardening, not a blocker: obj (from ToObject on a primitive `this`, which creates a fresh wrapper) is not rooted during the ops::length_of_array_like call, which runs before agent.with_roots. Getters on the prototype chain could allocate and trigger GC there. Consider rooting obj from step 1 onward, or confirm that the GC cannot collect it at that point. Please also check the change under KAHVI_GC_STRESS=1. The to_clamped_index helper is a local copy because ops lacks ToClampedIndex/ToAbsoluteIndex. Other built-ins (copyWithin, slice, splice, at-like) would need it too, so the helper belongs in ops eventually. The doc comment saying "only this built-in needs it so far" is inaccurate.
